Lo Shu Grid calculator

Place the digits of your date of birth on the 3×3 Lo Shu square and see which numbers are strong and which are missing.

Lo Shu Grid Calculator
Places the digits of your date of birth onto the classic 3×3 Lo Shu magic square.

What the Lo Shu Grid is

The Lo Shu square is a 3×3 magic square from Chinese tradition in which every row, column and diagonal adds up to 15. In numerology it is used as a fixed map: each of the numbers 1 to 9 has its own position on the grid.

The calculator takes every non-zero digit in your date of birth and places it in its position. A number that appears twice in your birth date appears twice in its box, and a box that stays empty is a missing number.

How the grid is read

Numerologists look at repeated numbers as areas of strength and missing numbers as qualities you may need to work at. They also read complete rows and lines, such as the line of 4, 5 and 6. The grid is a simple tool, and an experienced numerologist will read it together with your Life Path Number rather than on its own.

Frequently asked

Common questions

Why are zeros left out of the grid?

The Lo Shu square holds only the numbers 1 to 9, so a zero in your date of birth has no position and is not placed.

What does a missing number mean?

It is usually read as a quality that does not come naturally and may take more conscious effort. It is not a flaw, and most people have several missing numbers.

Is the Lo Shu Grid the same as my Life Path Number?

No. Both come from your date of birth, but the grid shows which digits appear and how often, while the Life Path Number reduces them all to one number.
